questions.q: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: decide the fate of
questions.s:
The segment with the grammatical error is "are here to."

The correct form should be "is here to" because "committee" is a collective noun, which is typically treated as singular. Thus, the sentence should read: "Most of the committee is here to decide the fate of this ancient building."

questions.q: At the concert, a choir of singers performed a beautiful rendition of a classic hymn.
questions.s: In the sentence provided, "a choir of singers" is the appropriate phrase to describe a group of vocalists performing together. Therefore, "no improvement" is the correct choice.

questions.q: The school carnival raised significant proceeds for new playground equipments.
questions.s:
The word "equipment" is an uncountable noun. Some uncountable nouns are "furniture," "water," “knowledge,” and "information." When using uncountable nouns, they typically do not change form to indicate plural or singular. Instead, the word "equipment" remains the same whether you're referring to one piece of equipment or many.

Therefore, the correct way to refer to multiple pieces of playground equipment is simply "equipment," not "equipments." So, in the corrected sentence, "equipment" remains singular despite referring to multiple items.

questions.q: The committee have submitted its reports to the director yesterday.
questions.s: "Committee" is a collective noun that takes a singular verb. The correct form should be "has submitted" not "have submitted". The sentence should read: "The committee has submitted its report to the director yesterday.”

questions.q: The session court has issued two summons against him/but he / has not attended to any of them. / No error
o: The session court has issued two summons against him
has not attended to any of them.
questions.s:
The word “summons” is singular in form but pluralized as “summonses.”
So, when talking about more than one, we must say “two summonses.”
Correct Sentence:The sessions court has issued two summonses against him, but he has not attended to any of them.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the highlighted word(s) in the given sentence.
o: sceneries in Darjeeling had been
scenery in Darjeeling is
sceneries in Darjeeling is
scenery in Darjeeling were
questions.s:
Answer:scenery in Darjeeling is

Explanation:
The word "scenery" is an uncountable noun, so it does not take a plural form like "sceneries." Hence, "sceneries" is incorrect.

Also, since we're talking about a general fact in the present, the verb should be "is", not "were" or "had been."

Let’s evaluate the options:

  • sceneries in Darjeeling had been – ❌ "sceneries" is incorrect; "had been" is past perfect – also incorrect

  • scenery in Darjeeling is – ✅ Correct: uncountable noun + correct present tense verb

  • sceneries in Darjeeling is – ❌ "sceneries" is incorrect

  • scenery in Darjeeling were – ❌ "scenery" is singular, so "were" is incorrect

Correct sentence:
The scenery in Darjeeling is breathtaking.

questions.q:
In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option.

He stood on the (A)/ street corner, haranguing (B)/ passer-bys about the stupidity (C)/ of the forthcoming war. (D)
questions.s:
Part C has an error.

A compound noun forms plural by making the principal word plural. For example, 'Daughter-in-laws' is incorrect; the correct plural form of 'daughter-in-law' is 'daughters-in-law'. Similarly, the plural form of 'passer-by' (a person who happens to be going past something, especially on foot) is 'passers-by'.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: He stood on the street corner, haranguing passers-by about the stupidity of the forthcoming war.

questions.q:
Sal trees have been planted in relatively three-fourth of the forest area.

(CGL tier -II 2022)
questions.s:
correct answer is: (4) nearly three-fourths


The fraction "three-fourths" refers to three parts out of four and must always be written in plural form (-s) because it indicates a portion greater than one.

  • "Three-fourths" is a fractional noun that indicates three out of four parts.

Corrected Sentence: Sal trees have been planted in nearly three-fourths of the forest area.
